title: Claudia shell contract, version 1
description: The messages that the Claudia web frontend (the page) and a desktop shell (GTK on Linux, later Neutralino on Windows and macOS) may send each other (E5.12, D42). One message is one JSON object. Evolution inside a version is additive only: new optional fields and new message types may appear, a receiver ignores fields and message types it does not know. Anything else (a field removed, a meaning changed, a field made required) is a new version with its own schema file; shells say which versions they speak in 'welcome' and 'error'.

actionId.description: An action is named like a menu path in lower case: 'file.save', 'edit.undo', 'view.page'. Menus and ids come from the menu and action manifest of the shell (E5.1).

hello.description: Page to shell, first message: the page says which contract it speaks and which app it shows. A page that does not know yet which app its server runs (the server asks for a secret before it says) leaves 'app' out; the shell, which was connected to a server of its own app, takes it to be that app.

frontend.description: Version of the frontend, for diagnostics.

view.description: What the page is (sheet 11): 'start', the front page with no document open, for which a shell shows only the menu entries that work there; 'document', a document, for which it shows the whole menu. Left out by an older page, which gets the whole menu.

welcome.description: Shell to page, the answer to 'hello': the version both will speak, who the shell is and what it offers.

capabilities.description: What this shell offers. 'native-menu': the shell shows File, Edit, Tools and Help itself, the page should not draw its own menu bar. 'actions': the shell sends 'action' messages for its menu. 'connect': the shell connects to another server when the page sends 'connect' (the page does not navigate there itself: the shell keeps its view on one server's origin). 'servers': the shell keeps the list of servers and sends it as 'servers'; the page sends the list back when it changes. 'files' (D501): the shell chooses files of this computer for the page ('pick_file') and saves the page's files there ('save_file'), with its own dialogs.

locale.description: The shell's best guess at the person's locale (E5.7, D31), usually the OS locale. Optional, and never binding on the page: locale is always the client's own setting, and the page may have a stored override already.

app.description: The app this window is ('composes', 'computes', 'creates'), D444. Optional. On a server of several apps the page then shows this app's documents only and refuses files of another kind; without it the page shows every app, as in a browser tab.

setup_code.description: The setup code of the shell's own server while it has no administrator (D1373, SEC-12): the page shows the server settings without asking for it. Optional; only sent to a page of the shell's own server, never to a server the window was connected to.

ask_administrator.description: True for a page of the computer's shared service (E8.5, D1624) while it has no administrator and the person of this shell may not read its setup code: the page tells her that only an administrator of this computer can name the server's first administrator. Optional; never sent together with 'setup_code'.

action.description: Shell to page: the person chose a menu item (or pressed its accelerator) that the page has to carry out.

action_state.description: Page to shell: which actions are enabled, ticked, relabelled or left out right now (Undo is only enabled when there is something to undo), and which menus of the bar have nothing left. Only the actions named change. 'visible' and 'empty' came with the menus that show what fits (D1645): optional, so a shell that does not know them greys what is left out, which is safe.

visible.description: False: the entry is left out of the menus, not greyed (D1600). Its key still reaches the page, which says why.

empty.description: Every menu of the bar that has nothing left now, by its word in the definition in lower case ('insert'), with the greyed line that says why, in the person's language (D1603). It replaces what the shell knew: a menu not named has entries.

error.description: Either direction: a message could not be accepted.

supported.description: With 'unsupported_contract': the contract versions the sender speaks.

serverEntry.description: One server in the list that the shell remembers for an app. The shape of the web app's own bookmark.

custom.description: True once a person has named it: a refreshed default name no longer replaces it.

local.description: True for her own server on this computer ('Private on this computer', D1623), which the shell adds itself and never remembers.

shared.description: True for the computer's shared service ('Shared on this computer', E8.5, D1622), which the shell adds while it is installed; it remembers only a name a person gave it.

connect.description: Page to shell: the person asked to connect to the server at this address. The shell checks it (plain http only for this computer, the server answers, it serves this same app, its certificate) and then shows that server in this window, or answers 'connect_failed'.

connect_failed.description: Shell to page: the connection asked for with 'connect' was not made. 'message' is written for the person and already translated; 'code' says why.

servers.description: Either direction. Shell to page: the servers this app remembers, this computer's own first, sent after 'welcome'. Page to shell: the list after the person renamed a server or the page learned a name; it replaces the shell's list, except for this computer's own entry, which the shell never keeps.

fileRequest.description: The page's name for one file transfer, unique while it lasts; every message of the transfer carries it (D501).

pick_file.description: Page to shell (D501): the person wants a file of this computer. The shell shows its Open dialog, offering files with these extensions, and answers 'file_result': 'picked' (then the file in 'file_chunk' messages and a 'file_done'), 'cancelled' or 'failed'. Only sent when the shell offers 'files'.

accept.description: Extensions without the dot, lower case; empty for any file.

save_file.description: Page to shell (D501, D502): a file of 'size' bytes follows in 'file_chunk' messages and a 'file_done'. With 'purpose' 'save' (the default) the shell asks where to save it, suggesting 'name', and answers 'file_result' 'saved' with the path, 'cancelled' or 'failed'. With 'print' it asks nothing: it opens the file in the computer's viewer for its kind (a PDF), from where it is printed, and answers 'opened'. Only sent when the shell offers 'files'.

name.description: The file's name, without a folder.

file_chunk.description: Either direction (D501): one piece of the file of a transfer, in order from 0, as base64 (at most 48 KiB, so that the message stays within 64 KiB).

file_done.description: Either direction (D501): every piece of the file of a transfer has been sent; 'chunks' says how many.

offer_file.description: Shell to page (D505): the person dropped a file of this computer on the window, where the web view would not hand it to the page. The file follows in 'file_chunk' messages and a 'file_done' with this 'request' (a name the shell chose); the page takes it as if it had been dropped on it. Only sent by a shell that offers 'files'.

file_result.description: Shell to page (D501, D502): what became of a transfer. 'picked' comes before the pieces of the chosen file and names it ('name', 'size', and its full 'path', SEC-27); 'saved' and 'opened' give the 'path' it went to; 'cancelled' means the person closed the dialog; 'failed' has a 'message' fit to show to the person.
